answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the harbor: one stake locked on the home chain anchors each identity, and timbers from every linked chain must point to the same wallet. Any new chain adds a fee ripple that compounds 2x per binding. An attacker splitting one stake across five chains pays 1+2+4+8+16=31x base stake, while payoff stays flat—bleeding out before the third chain. It works because cost grows exponentially while sybil yield stays linear.
